arxiv-2106-03910.description: Abstract . We prove a logarithmic version of Fontaine’s classic result on differentials of 𝒪 K ¯ \mathcal{O}_{\bar{K}} over 𝒪 K \mathcal{O}_{K} . 1. Introduction Let K be a p -adic field, \bar{K} an algebraic closure and \mathbb{C}_{p}=\hat{\bar{K}} its completion. We denote by \mathcal{O}_{K} and \mathcal{O}_{\bar{K}} their rings of integers. The module of Kähler differentials \Omega=\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_{\bar{K}}/\mathcal{O}_{K}} is well-known.

arxiv-2108-06713.title: Channel State Acquisition in Uplink NOMA for Cellular-Connected UAV: Exploitation of Doppler and Modulation Diversities
arxiv-2108-06713.creator: DONATELLA DARSENA 1 (SENIOR MEMBER, IEEE), IVAN IUDICE 2 , AND FRANCESCO VERDE 1 (SENIOR MEMBER, IEEE)
arxiv-2108-06713.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by DONATELLA DARSENA 1 (SENIOR MEMBER, IEEE), IVAN IUDICE 2 , AND FRANCESCO VERDE 1 (SENIOR MEMBER, IEEE). Integration of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) for surveillance or monitoring applications into fifth generation (5G) New Radio (NR) cellular networks is an intriguing problem that has recently tackled a lot of interest in both academia and industry.

arxiv-2110-09009.title: Assessment of a porous viscoelastic model for wave attenuation in ice-covered seas Journal: …
arxiv-2110-09009.creator: Boyang Xu, Philippe Guyenne
arxiv-2110-09009.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Boyang Xu, Philippe Guyenne. [ 3 ] recently proposed a two-dimensional continuum model for linear gravity waves propagating in ice-covered seas. It is based on a two-layer formulation where the ice cover is viewed as a porous viscoelastic medium. In the present paper, extensive tests against both laboratory experiments and field observations are performed to assess this model’s ability at describing wave attenuation in various types of sea ice.

arxiv-2305-05030.title: Adaptive Cross Tubal Tensor Approximation Journal: Journal
arxiv-2305-05030.creator: Salman Ahmadi-Asl, Anh Huy Phan, Andrzej Cichocki, Anastasia Sozykina, Zaher Al Aghbari, Jun Wang, and Ivan Oseledets
arxiv-2305-05030.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new adaptive cross algorithm for computing a low tubal rank approximation of third-order tensors, with less memory and lower computational complexity than the truncated tensor SVD (t-SVD). This makes it applicable for decomposing large-scale tensors.

arxiv-2305-17428.title: Choosing the Right Weights: Balancing Value, Strategy, and Noise in Recommender Systems
arxiv-2305-17428.creator: Smitha Milli, Emma Pierson, Nikhil Garg
arxiv-2305-17428.description: Abstract . Many recommender systems optimize a linear weighting of different user behaviors, such as clicks, likes, and shares. We analyze the optimal choice of weights from the perspectives of both users and content producers who strategically respond to the weights.

arxiv-2312-17110.title: Toward Semantic Scene Understanding for Fine-Grained 3D Modeling of Plants
arxiv-2312-17110.creator: Mohamad Qadri, Harry Freeman, Eric Schneider, George Kantor
arxiv-2312-17110.description: Abstract Agricultural robotics is an active research area due to global population growth and expectations of food and labor shortages. Robots can potentially help with tasks such as pruning, harvesting, phenotyping, and plant modeling. However, agricultural automation is hampered by the difficulty in creating high resolution 3D semantic maps in the field that would allow for safe manipulation and navigation.

arxiv-2403-05624.creator: Ryan Hazlett, Mihir Kulkarni, Eli Visbal, John H. Wise
arxiv-2403-05624.description: Abstract We present a method that calibrates a semi-analytic model to the Renaissance Simulations , a suite of cosmological hydrodynamical simulations with high-redshift galaxy formation. This approach combines the strengths of semi-analytic techniques and hydrodynamical simulations, enabling the extension to larger volumes and lower redshifts inaccessible to simulations due to computational expense.

arxiv-2404-19204.title: NeRF-Insert: Local 3D Editing with Multimodal Control Signals
arxiv-2404-19204.creator: Benet Oriol Sabat, Alessandro Achille, Matthew Trager, Stefano Soatto
arxiv-2404-19204.description: Abstract We propose NeRF-Insert, a NeRF editing framework that allows users to make high-quality local edits with a flexible level of control. Unlike previous work that relied on image-to-image models, we cast scene editing as an in-painting problem, which encourages the global structure of the scene to be preserved.

arxiv-2412-18567.title: Production of η b \eta_{b} in ultra-peripheral P ​ b ​ P ​ b PbPb collisions
arxiv-2412-18567.creator: C.N. Azevedo 1 , F.C. Sobrinho 1 , F.S. Navarra 1 1 Instituto de Física, Universidade de São Paulo, Rua do Matão 1371 - CEP 05508-090, Cidade Universitária, São Paulo, SP, Brazil
arxiv-2412-18567.description: Abstract Very recently, the two-photon decay width of the η b \eta_{b} meson was computed with lattice QCD methods. This decay has not yet been measured. The knowledge of this width allows for the calculation of the η b \eta_{b} production cross section through photon-photon interactions in ultraperipheral P ​ b ​ P ​ b PbPb collisions.

arxiv-2505-09605.title: The Niche Connectivity Paradox: Multichrome Contagions Overcome Vaccine Hesitancy more effectively than Monochromacy
arxiv-2505-09605.creator: Ho-Chun Herbert Chang, Feng Fu
arxiv-2505-09605.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ho-Chun Herbert Chang, Feng Fu. The rise of vaccine hesitancy has caused a resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles and pertussis, alongside widespread skepticism and refusals of COVID-19 vaccinations during the COVID-19 pandemic. While categorizing individuals as either supportive of or opposed to vaccines provides a convenient dichotomy of vaccine attitudes and behaviors, the issue of vaccine hesitancy is far more complex and dynamic.

arxiv-2511-19496.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yang Liu Xiaolong Zhong Ling Jiang. Large language models deliver strong reasoning and tool-use skills, yet their computational demands make them impractical for edge or cost-sensitive deployments. We present Xmodel-2.5 , a 1.3-billion-parameter small language model designed as a drop-in agent core . Training with maximal-update parameterization ( μ \mu P) allows hyper-parameters tuned on a 20M-parameter proxy to transfer directly to the full model, even under the parameter-tied tie-word-embedding architecture.

pmc-10738910.title: CONCORDANCE IN SPOUSES’ INTENTION TO MOVE AFTER RETIREMENT AMONG KOREAN MIDDLE-AGED COUPLES
pmc-10738910.creator: Eunju Lee, Kyungmin Kim
pmc-10738910.description: Midlife adults often envision life after retirement and start planning for retirement, forming their own expectations of where they live after retirement. Migration after retirement is an important decision in that physical and social environments of housing and communities affect health and well-being in later life.

pmc-10765181.title: The Need for Vestibular Implants in a Tertiary Referral Ear, Nose, and Throat Center and Its Relation to Hearing Status
pmc-10765181.creator: Morgana Sluydts, Julie Elen, Sandrien Mertens, Nadia Verstraeten, Kathleen Verhaegen, Erwin Offeciers, Joost JS van Dinther, Andrzej Zarowski, Floris L Wuyts
pmc-10765181.description: Background:Patients with bilateral vestibulopathy (BVP) are at increased risk of falling and have poor quality of life. Several research groups are currently developing and investigating vestibular implants to treat BVP. The goal was to identify how many patients can be considered eligible for vestibular implantation.

pmc-11544561.title: Delta‐like ligand 4 inhibitor drug treatment induces pulmonary hypertension in cancer clinical trials
pmc-11544561.creator: Casandra E Besse, Nolan M Winicki, Cristian Puerta, Moises Hernandez, Jason X‐J Yuan, Patricia A Thistlethwaite
pmc-11544561.description: Delta‐like ligand 4 (DLL‐4) inhibitor drugs are an emerging cancer treatment. In clinical trials for solid organ malignancies, intravenous administration of monoclonal antibodies that inhibit DLL‐4 is associated with development of pulmonary hypertension, in the absence of left ventricular dysfunction. Analysis of 13 clinical trials showed that pulmonary hypertension is a complication of DLL‐4 inhibition.

Credit: Love Dalén/Stockholm University. “What we were looking at was, in some sense, a piece of mammoth jerky,” says Olga Dudchenko, an applied physicist and mathematician working in genomics at Baylor College of Medicine. It also causes the N and O glycosylation of proteins in the Trans Golgi area.

pmc-12656670.title: Eliminating Measles: Factors That Contribute to Re-Establishing Transmission
pmc-12656670.creator: Emily Gibson, David N. Durrheim, Patrick O’Connor
pmc-12656670.description: Background/Objectives: Since 2016, 14 countries previously verified to have eliminated endemic measles transmission have lost their elimination status. To explore whether there were identifiable risk factors for re-establishing measles transmission in these countries, a narrative review of the literature was undertaken.

pmc-12702508.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of QT Prolongation and Torsades de Pointes following Intravenous Amiodarone Administration for Atrial Fibrillation: A Cohort Study
pmc-12702508.creator: Yuttana Wongsalap, Waruni Miliam, Suparpish Deesham, Arissara Thepsaen, Aphatsara Churasae, Duangkamon Poolpun, Tomon Thongsri, Niwat Saksit
pmc-12702508.description: Introduction:Amiodarone has been reported to be associated with QTc interval prolongation and Torsades de pointes (TdP). This study aimed to assess the incidence and identify the risk factors of QTc prolongation and TdP associated with intravenous amiodarone therapy in patients diagnosed with atrial fibrillation (AF).

pmc-13148660.title: Four moral models of global health security
pmc-13148660.creator: Frances Charlotte Butcher, Patricia Kingori, Michael Parker
pmc-13148660.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Global health security is concerned with the response to infectious disease outbreaks across international borders. However, its precise nature and scope are contested because of lack of agreement about its focus and beneficiaries. Informed by qualitative interviews with thirty-eight professionals working in the field, this article explores views on how the scope and boundaries of global health security should be understood.

pmc-13149032.title: Single-cell spatiotemporal dissection of the human maternal–fetal interface
pmc-13149032.creator: Cheng Wang, Yan Zhou, Yuejun Wang, Tuhin Kumar Guha, Zhida Luo, Anxhela Mustafaraj, Tara I McIntyre, Marisa E Schwab, Brittany R Davidson, Gabriella C Reeder, Ronald J Wong, Sarah K England, Juan M Gonzalez, Robert Blelloch, Alexis J Combes, Linda C Giudice, Adrian Erlebacher, Tippi C MacKenzie, Dav
pmc-13149032.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The human maternal–fetal interface is characterized by mosaic intermingling of maternal and fetal cells1. Yet the underlying cellular, molecular and spatial programmes remain incompletely defined. Here we generate a comprehensive atlas of the human maternal–fetal interface across normal pregnancies from early gestation to term by integrating large-scale paired single-nucleus transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling with submicrometre-resolution spatial transcriptomics and CODEX multiplex protein imaging2, substantially boosting the spatiotemporal resolution of prior research3.

pmc-13208539.title: Comparison of Three International Definitions for Overweight and Obesity in a Population of Adolescents in Greece
pmc-13208539.creator: Eleni M. Domouzoglou, Evangelia E. Ntzani, Michail I. Papafaklis, Anastasios Serbis, Ekaterini Siomou, Flora Bacopoulou, Assimina Galli-Tsinopoulou
pmc-13208539.description: Background: Early diagnosis of obesity in adolescents is crucial for the prevention of severe health consequences. Different criteria for the diagnosis of obesity may lead to variations in prevalence. We aimed to compare the three most widely used international definitions (by WHO, IOTF and CDC) for overweight/obesity in adolescents in Northwestern Greece.

pmc-13448641.title: Development and characterization of a sustainable bacterial cellulose/collagen composite membrane for enhanced wound healing and tissue regeneration applications
pmc-13448641.creator: Hanaa Orabi, Manal Shalaby, Ebtesam Naeim Hussieny, Monira Zhran, Yousra A. El-Maradny, Esmail M. El-Fkharany
pmc-13448641.description: This study aimed to develop a bacterial cellulose/collagen composite membrane (BC/COL) for its wound-healing ability using collagen extracted from the scales of golden grouper (Epinephelus coioides), thus providing a sustainable derived source. BC was produced by Acetobacter pasteurianus PV549389 under static fermentation, and culture conditions were optimized using response surface methodology.

pmc-13556674.creator: C Cruceanu
pmc-13556674.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPsychological distress like anxiety or depression and life events like trauma or natural disasters play important roles in maternal and fetal health in pregnancy. According to the developmental origins of health and disease hypothesis, and consistent with perinatal longitudinal studies, the interplay of genetic predispositions with a wide range of environmental exposures individual differences in developmental trajectories and health risk outcomes of offspring.
